page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-32-lssd is an arm64 general-purpose server configuration built on 32 dedicated ARMv8 Neoverse-V2 physical cores operating at 3.0 GHz. The processor architecture allocates one hardware thread per core, backed by 64 KB of L1 data cache and 2 MB of L2 cache per core alongside an 80 MB shared L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 128 GB, yielding a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per core. The instance includes 2412 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage to support high-throughput I/O requirements.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong memory throughput and multi-threaded scaling. The server placed in the top tier for Geekbench multi-core performance with a score of 23030.0 and Passmark database operations with 49685.86. Memory subsystem performance is supported by uncached read bandwidth reaching 345.42 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 163.3 GB/sec. Application-level metrics reflect these capabilities, producing 69.35 million Redis SET operations per second and 77.9 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

The dedicated physical core architecture provides deterministic processing without noisy-neighbor contention from hyperthreading, yielding strong resource efficiency for concurrent compute pipelines. A primary tradeoff involves the ARM architecture, which omits x86-oriented instruction sets such as AVX-512 and AMX, and the configuration does not include discrete GPUs. The hardware configuration makes this server type appropriate for production database systems, distributed caching tiers like Redis, high-concurrency web serving, and software compilation tasks.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-32-lssd is a general-purpose server powered by a 32-core ARMv8 Neoverse-V2 processor clocked at 3.0 GHz, 128 GB of memory, and 2412 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage. Operating with one dedicated thread per physical core, the instance provides consistent execution without hyperthreading overhead. Benchmark testing indicates top-tier performance in multi-core workloads, Passmark memory throughput, and database operational benchmarks. Memory performance remains strong, with uncached large-block reads achieving 345.42 GB/sec, supporting Redis workloads at 69.35 million operations per second and web serving throughput of 77.9 GB/sec. While the platform does not include GPU acceleration or x86-specific vector extensions, its balanced memory footprint, dedicated core allocation, and fast local storage make it suitable for low-latency databases, in-memory caches, software compilation, and high-concurrency web applications.
